newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Chretien may discuss ag -- USDA official.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Chretien may discuss ag -- USDA official.

text.p: Agricultural trade disputes may come up at this week's meeting of President Clinton and Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien, a U.S. Agriculture Department official said Monday.
"There are issues which could be raised legitimately at that level," the USDA official told Reuters, adding he was not certain agriculture would be on the agenda.
No informal agricultural trade meetings were scheduled among senior U.S. and Canadian aides.
A U.S.-Canada bilateral meeting on agriculture was under consideration, the USDA official said, and might be held in the next month or so.
Canada and the United States are competitors in some markets as well agricultural export customers of each other.

The nations disagree on several points, among them Canada's system for making grain export sales, its wheat shipments to U.S. buyers and Canadian rules that limit imports of U.S. dairy and livestock products.
